articles.title: Keenan Allen changed Ashton Dulin's role. Now the Colts may use him everywhere.
articles.summary: Veteran Ashton Dulin has been the Colts' No. 2 healthy receiver in training game but may drop to No. 4, opening up roles on special teams.
articles.body:
Brian Mason has never been shy in his views of Ashton Dulin 's performance on special teams, calling the 29-year-old receiver veteran "one of the three-best special teams players in the NFL" last fall.

How much the Colts will be able to take advantage of those skills – on his most active days, Indianapolis uses his 4.4 speed as its primary gunner on punt coverage, as well as one of its two returners on kickoffs – may vary week-to-week, depending on the team's health across the board.

After last week's signing of six-time Pro Bowl receiver Keenan Allen , Dulin finds himself no longer in contention for one of the Colts ' three starting wideout spots. Instead he's jockeying with Nick Westbrook-Ikhine for fourth on the depth chart on a team whose star second-year tight end Tyler Warren makes Dulin or Westbrook-Ikhine the fifth receiving option at-best.

NFL preseason; Indianapolis Colts against Atlanta Falcons

Dulin has performed arguably the most consistently of Indianapolis' rotational wideouts in the preseason, all while taking very few reps on special teams. It gave the appearance the Colts planned to significantly reduce his role on punt and kick teams to preserve his energy and impact for offense. But with Allen's signing dropping Dulin a spot, the receiver who has just seven catches since the end of the 2022 campaign finds himself in virtually the same spot as the end of last season.

"How many phases and plays he gets on special teams will just be dictated by how many plays (the offensive coaches) anticipate him getting in a game," Colts special teams coordinator Brian Mason told reporters Monday. "We usually meet at the beginning of a regular season game week, and we'll kinda project who'll be up for the week and how much they plan to play.

"If they say, 'He's going to play this number of plays' on offense, that will then determine whether he plays in one, two or three phases on special teams."

As Mason went on to explain, the Colts plan to look at Dulin as a potential punt returner this week, among a long list of kick return spots. Among players in the NFL in 2025 with more than one kickoff return attempt, Dulin's 32.3-yard average ranked third-best in the league, but in the background, Mason said Dulin has been working on his punt return skills for two years.

Through two preseason games, second-year receiver Coleman Owen has been the Colts' most consistent and active returner on kicks and punts, with rookie running back Seth McGowan and rookie receiver Deion Burks , shuffling through in preseason action. Incumbent starting returner Anthony Gould has been out for much of camp with a groin injury, while the team lost frequent returner Ameer Abdullah in free agency. Josh Downs has taken reps on punt return, but the team would like to limit that given his increasing role in the offense.

Mason went on to explain that Dulin's lack of special teams reps throughout training camp came, in part, so the team could evaluate its young fringe roster players to narrow in on final contenders for various roles he would be a finalist for, pending his responsibilities on offense.

"We planned on using Ashton Dulin in roles no matter what, whether that be on kick return or at gunner. If he ever needs a sub at gunner, we can always give him a sub, but we certainly still want to have the threat of being able to use him and our opponent knowing there's a good chance he still may be out there," Mason said. "I think that does affect certain people's punt return game plan.

"If Ashton Dulin is on the field for the punt team, you certainly have to account for him and you certainly need to probably (double-team) him in order to prevent him from causing problems."

articles.title: ‘Made it easy’ – Carlos Alcaraz praises Serena Williams after US Open mixed doubles appearance
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz and Serena Williams crashed out of US Open mixed doubles, but not before getting an impressive win. Alcaraz had great things to say about the...
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz and Serena Williams crashed out of US Open mixed doubles, but not before getting an impressive win. Alcaraz had great things to say about the legendary Williams after their victory.

The US Open mixed doubles event has seen some glamorous pairings. Aryna Sabalenka and Novak Djokovic participated, and Carlos Alcaraz played alongside Serena Williams.

Sabalenka and Djokovic faced an upset in the first round, but Williams and Alcaraz managed to make it all the way to the quarter-finals.

They recorded a win against Lloyd Glasspool and Erin Routliffe in the Round of 16 before succumbing to Flavio Cobolli and Belinda Bencic in the quarter-finals.

Carlos Alcaraz says Serena Williams helped him with his nervousness in mixed doubles game

The duo won their game in the Round of 16 with a score of 5-3 and 4-1. After a tough first set, they got the job done with ease in the second.

Alcaraz is playing for the first time since his wrist injury in April kept him out of multiple major tournaments this year. And he praised Williams for being a calming presence for him.

"Everyone could see how nervous I was," Alcaraz said. "I made a double fault on the first point. I was really, really nervous….

"I was out for almost five months. I almost forgot how it felt to step on court once again. (The nervousness) was just for a couple of games, then Serena made it easy for me."

The duo may be out of the tournament already, but they drew a lot of attention with their performance. Now all eyes will be on Alcaraz to see how the Spaniard plays when the men's singles begin.

articles.title: Arsenal verbally agree club-record £56.5m sale
articles.summary: Al Hilal and Arsenal have reached a verbal agreement for the club-record transfer of Gabriel Martinelli, according to reports.Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Im...
articles.body:
Al Hilal and Arsenal have reached a verbal agreement for the club-record transfer of Gabriel Martinelli , according to reports.

James Benge of CBS Sports reported on Tuesday that Al Hilal and Arsenal were closing in on an agreement for the transfer of Gabriel Martinelli , with the fee expected to be around €58m (£49.7m) guaranteed, with €8m (£6.9m) in further bonuses.

The total package of £56.5m would represent a club-record sale for Arsenal, but Benge added that it's all subject to the player's final approval.

Sami Mokbel then confirmed for the BBC that Arsenal are closing in on a minimum £50m deal to sell Martinelli, with talks advanced and a conclusion imminent ahead of the winger making a formal decision.

Tom Canton reports for Football.London that a sell-on clause in the deal is one of many aspects of the deal being finalised in the last 24 hours, with Benge also previously reporting that the Gunners were looking to include such a clause in the deal.

Fabrizio Romano writes this morning that the player's agent is in direct contact with Al Hilal to seal an agreement on personal terms.

Romano confirms that a package worth over €65m has been verbally agreed between the two clubs, so it's all up to the player now.

Martinelli has been a key player for Arsenal over the last seven years, making 278 appearances and scoring 62 goals from his spot on the left wing.

The 25-year-old has won the Premier League, the FA Cup, and the Community Shield, and he extended his contract on a couple of occasions amid intense interest from elsewhere.

But the last couple of weeks have made it clear Mikel Arteta no longer intends to give the winger significant minutes, leaving him out of the matchday squads against Manchester City and Coventry City . It seems he's now on the verge of a move to the Saudi Pro League.

articles.title: 'Just fantastic with people.' Tom O'Brien had a lifelong connection with Cathedral
articles.summary: Tom O'Brien was coaching at the college level in 1967 when he came back to coach at Cathedral, his alma mater. He maintained longtime connection.
articles.body:
Tom O'Brien was a college basketball assistant at Bradley in 1967 when the opportunity arose to come back to coach at Cathedral, his alma mater.

O'Brien would leave a couple different times as coach, but never really did give up his connection to the school where he graduated from in 1949. O'Brien died on Aug. 17 at age 95.

"Tom had such a history with Cathedral, graduating from there and all the changes the school went through in good times and bad times, Tom was always part of it," said Steve Hodgson, who coached with O'Brien and then later succeeded him. "It goes even beyond that. There are so many families in the Catholic and Eastside community and people that I've heard from in the last week through Tom's passing that he touched."

O'Brien not only coached football, basketball and baseball at Cathedral, he later returned as a substitute and earned the nickname "Super Sub."

"Tom left a profound impact on Cathedral, both as a student and when he returned as an educator and coach," Cathedral shared on its social media accounts. "'Coach OB' coached football, basketball and baseball at Cathedral, leaving a lasting legacy on thousands of Cathedral students. During the final years of his tenure at Cathedral, he was affectionately known as 'Super Sub,' and students were always thrilled to see him walk through the classroom door."

O'Brien, who played football at Butler for legendary coach Tony Hinkle, coached on the staff at Evansville College for Arad McCutchan, helping the Aces to a perfect season in 1964-65. That team was led by Larry Humes and Jerry Sloan. But after coaching at Evansville and Bradley, O'Brien was drawn home with the opportunity to coach basketball at Cathedral.

After leading Cathedral to a 71-27 record over a four-year period, including the program's first sectional championship in 1971, O'Brien also served as the Marion County Clerk from 1975-79 before he was rehired as Cathedral's coach in 1979.

"He was a really, really good coach," said Brad Lennon, who was hired as O'Brien's freshman team coach in 1980 and coached on his staff the next six seasons. "He wasn't necessarily a master technician but he was a players' coach. He had a heart of gold and would do anything for anybody – just fantastic with people."

Steve Hodgson remembered one afternoon when O'Brien was feeling sick and was not going to be able to make it to a game at Center Grove. He spent 45 minutes talking on the phone to Hodgson, his assistant at Cathedral, about the game plan for the night. Just before the tipoff, O'Brien showed up at the game, saying he was "feeling better and coming to support the kids."

"I turned to Brad and said the over/under on him sitting on this bench is halftime," Hodgson said with a laugh. "I missed it by a quarter. If he was there, he was going to coach. I'd probably be the same way."

O'Brien's best team was the 1981-82 group led by senior Ken Barlow and junior Scott Hicks, both of whom would go on to Notre Dame; Shelton Smith (Wisconsin) and Carl Daniels (Rice). Cathedral was 27-2 going into the Final Four but ran into a buzzsaw in Scott Skiles and Plymouth, falling 62-59 in the afternoon game. Plymouth would beat Gary Roosevelt 75-74 in double overtime for the state championship that night.

"It was a tremendous experience for the kids to play in a packed Market Square Arena," Hodgson said. "We were probably the proverbial favorites. I remember in the locker room after the game, Tom talked to the kids about how it was one day in their lives. He told them they had an incredible season and were able to go to the Final Four ... all the great things they accomplished. Even though he was heartbroken and we all were, I appreciated those comments."

O'Brien stepped down in 1984. He coached nine seasons total at Cathedral, compiling a 164-60 record. He would go on to coach at Blackford in 1986 after two years working in the Marion County Sheriff's Department. O'Brien would later be a Sagamore of the Wabash recipient and an inaugural member of the Cathedral Circle of Excellence. On his 80th birthday, Mayor Greg Ballard declared it "Tom O'Brien Day" in Indianapolis.

"I might not have gotten into coaching if it wasn't for OB," Lennon said. "He was really good about letting you have your two cents as an assistant coach. Just a great guy with a great sense of humor. I owe him a lot."

O'Brien is proceeded in death by his wife, Marilyn O'Brien, his parents, five brothers James, Robert, Jack, Michael, Bernard and sisters Mary O'Brien and Patricia Norton. He is survived by his daughters, Dorothy (Pete) Miller, Kathleen Allgood and sister Barbara (Joseph) Minatel as well as many nieces and nephews.

Visitation will be held on Wednesday from 4-8 p.m. at Feeney-Hornak Keystone Mortuary, 2126 E. 71st Street. A Mass of Christian Burial will be held on Thursday at 11 a.m. at St. Lawrence Catholic Church 6944 E. 46th Street, with burial to follow in Westridge Park Cemetery.

Memorial contributions go to Cathedral Tuition Assistance Fund, 5225 E. 56th St., Indianapolis, IN 46226.

articles.title: 🚨 Reports: nearly €60m obligation, Marmoush leaves City again
articles.summary: Just one year after his move to Manchester City, Omar Marmoush already appears to be on the move again. The Egyptian is reportedly set to join Tottenham in L...
articles.body:
Just one year after his move to Manchester City, Omar Marmoush already appears to be on the move again. The Egyptian is reportedly set to join Tottenham in London from the Citizens on loan. That is being reported by 'The Athletic' and Florian Plettenberg alike.

According to Plettenberg, the loan could also become an obligation to buy under certain circumstances. If that clause is triggered, Spurs would likely have to send £50 million to Manchester, which is roughly equivalent to €58 million.

Incidentally, Eintracht will not receive any share of the deal, according to matching reports from Plettenberg and Sven Michel.

Reports claiming that Man City had wanted to structure Marmoush's price in a certain way to avoid a sell-on payment to Frankfurt are "nonsense," Plettenberg's side says.

Marmoush is reportedly set to undergo his medical later today before being officially unveiled. As David Ornstein reports, he has already said goodbye to his City teammates.

articles.title: Jaissle set to get his wish with Gonzalez
articles.summary: Although Newcastle's young side came within seconds of defeating Liverpool on the opening weekend, there was always going to be work to do before the window...
articles.body:
Although Newcastle 's young side came within seconds of defeating Liverpool on the opening weekend, there was always going to be work to do before the window shut on 1 September.

Newcastle have made six signings so far this summer in goalkeepers Lukas Hornicek and Ewen Jaouen, defender Amar Dedic, midfielders Aladji Bamba and Sean Steur and forward Bazoumana Toure.

But Matthias Jaissle made it clear that "adjustments need to be done and will be" in an interview with BBC Sport last week.

After reluctantly selling talisman Guimaraes to Arsenal , Nico Gonzalez possesses the qualities Newcastle have been looking for in the middle of the park.

This is a player who would have been potentially out of reach not so long ago.

Of those midfielders who played a minimum of 900 minutes in Europe's top five leagues last season, Gonzalez led the way for high turnovers per game (2.13).

He also ranked in the Premier League's top five midfielders for line-breaking passes per match (12).

Those traits - in and out of possession - could make Gonzalez an invaluable addition as he is handed a greater role at St James' Park.

articles.title: What would Marmoush give Spurs?
articles.summary: Omar Marmoush is primarily a number nine, but he has rarely been confined to one role across the front line.  Manchester City have followed a similar pattern...
articles.body:
Omar Marmoush is primarily a number nine, but he has rarely been confined to one role across the front line.

At Frankfurt, he was used predominantly through the middle but also appeared as a second striker and from the left. Manchester City have followed a similar pattern, using him mainly as a central attacker while also deploying him from the flank and just behind another forward.

That flexibility could suit Roberto de Zerbi. His teams have often relied on forwards changing positions, dropping towards the ball and then attacking the space created when opponents are drawn out. Marmoush is comfortable doing both.

Former Manchester City defender Nedum Onuoha sees the Egyptian as most dangerous when he is able to threaten the space beyond the defence.

"As much as he is good dropping towards the ball, I think he is better when he plays on the shoulder," he said.

"He needs to be in a team that will constantly play balls in behind and force the opposition to run back towards their own goal. That's when you see a better version of Marmoush."

Opta's Premier League numbers from last season show he averaged 11.46 runs in behind per 90 minutes, almost identical to Dominic Solanke 's 11.61 and ahead of Richarlison 's 10.03. But he also offered considerably more with the ball.

articles.title: Bills overlooked defensive back making a strong preseason impression
articles.summary: Second-year defensive back Jordan Hancock is giving Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard plenty to evaluate because of his versatility.
articles.body:
ORCHARD PARK - Given how the Buffalo Bills brought so many new players into their defensive secondary, both via the draft and free agency, it almost felt like Jordan Hancock was a forgotten man.

Contributing to that dynamic is that it was a bit of out of sight, out of mind for Hancock during the spring because in addition to the arrivals of free agents CJ Gardner-Johnson , Geno Stone , and Dee Alford , and draft picks Davison Igbinosun , Jalon Kilgore and Toriano Pride joining the team, Hancock missed all of the on-field portions of the offseason program recovering from shoulder surgery.

But through this point in training camp and the first two preseason games, if anyone truly had forgotten about the 2025 fifth-round pick , he's reminding everyone exactly who he is.

"It's cool to see because it's a guy who didn't get an offseason at all and, in a new system, that's really hard," coach Joe Brady said. "It's good to see a guy coming off an injury, there's no hesitation, flying around, making plays. He's figuring out what that niche is, and we're asking a lot of him, moving him around. Our nickel plays a lot of different roles, so to be able to play safety, play nickel, help on special teams. It was cool to see him finally make some plays."

A delayed start but fast climb for Jordan Hancock

Through the first two preseason games according to Pro Football Focus charting, Hancock has played 57 total snaps, 38 of those as a slot corner and 17 at free safety, plus two random snaps on the line. He's been in on five tackles and every one of them was regarded as a "stop" which PFF defines as a tackle that caused a failure for the offense. Although he has allowed five receptions on six targets, those have gone for just 12 yards total.

"I told you he was going to be one of the biggest evaluations this camp because he did miss the offseason," defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard said. "Any time you have guys who missed snaps on the field, you have to play a little bit of catch up as far as the evaluation and he's doing a great job.

"It's finding the right amount of snaps, the right roles for him. Obviously he has to be a little bit of a Swiss Army knife right now as far as learning safety, learning the nickel position. There are other sub grouping packages that we can get him in and do different things that are kind of that hybrid type of role as well. He's handling it well."

Why versatility matters in Jim Leonhard's defense

Hancock was not a factor in the first half of 2025 but he started getting playing time in the blowout Week 8 victory over Carolina and was active for every game thereafter with the exception of Week 17 against the Eagles and the divisional round playoff loss to the Broncos .

He played 398 total snaps, including special teams. Of those, 183 came on defense, with most of that work at free safety and only six snaps in the slot. This year in Leonhard's defense, the slot corner will be deployed differently than it was over the last several seasons when Taron Johnson occupied the role on nearly every snap.

Leonhard is going to play matchups and will use Alford as the primary starter, but he will rotate others in depending on who lines up across that position, and Hancock could be in the mix.

"It helps a lot," Hancock said of being versatile. "I planted my seed last year and was growing and growing every day with both positions being versatile. I feel like I just got on the field, I played more than I was expected to play. I had opportunities, whether I made the play or not, I had the opportunity to be out there. Now to be in a position where I have to play either position, safety or nickel, I'm trying to be the best at both spots for sure."

The 6-foot, 195-pounder is a dynamic athlete. Basketball was his first love growing up outside Atlanta - his favorite player was Russell Westbrook - and he could dunk a basketball when he stood just 5-foot-7 as an eighth grader, though he could just as easily drop a bomb from three-point range.

It was Mel Tucker, who was the defensive coordinator at Georgia and later the head coach at Michigan State, who after seeing him at football practice while on the recruiting trail told Hancock that football should be his primary sport.

That didn't pay off for Tucker because Ohio State swooped in and signed Hancock and he went on to play 42 games for the Buckeyes totaling 98 tackles, 2.5 sacks, three interceptions, 14 passes defensed and four forced fumbles.

"Just being at Ohio State, just being around great people, great coaches," he said regarding his pedigree playing in a big-time program and how that helped his transition to the NFL. "You're not bigger than anybody. There's always room for improvement and I feel like that's with me, I feel like improvement is a lot. I feel like I can improve and develop, and I'm ready to learn and ready to compete."

Bills looking for answers beyond the starters

In addition to being a physical player, Hancock has the ability to quickly diagnose what's happening, though he does have a tendency to play almost too fast and it gets him out of position. Often, he can recover, but occasionally he doesn't and especially at safety, that can be dangerous.

"He's a confident player," Leonhard said of the former Ohio State standout who played for the Buckeyes' 2024 national championship team. "He's going to make quick decisions and play fast, he's going to make mistakes. There are things that aren't always clean, but he makes fast decisions and he's going to live with the results. You respect that as a coach. You have to take some of the hard edges off sometimes, but you do know he's going to impact the game and he's going to fly around and he's going to set the tone."

Unless there are injuries, Hancock isn't going to be a starter for Buffalo, but if he continues to play the way he has this summer, he's going to get a game-day jersey.

"Every game you get into and there's a situation that pops up where you're one injury or you're one guy having a bad performance away from a lot of pieces moving around," Leonhard said.

"That's always the fun part of being a coach in the NFL is you only have a limited amount of bodies. You get into games and sometimes there's a guy backing up multiple positions and how you're going to play that out and making adjustments, maybe something you thought was going to work well going into the game, you're not getting production out of it and you have to make adjustments. It's huge for me having a handful of guys you know have a flexible skill set. The more players you have in different groups like that, the better."

Sal Maiorana has covered the Buffalo Bills for more than four decades including 37 years as the full-time beat writer/columnist for the D&C. articles.summary: Cody Gakpo Transfer Latest as Tottenham and Manchester City Monitor Liverpool ForwardThe latest transfer discussion from Fabrizio Romano placed Cody Gakpo fi...
articles.body:
Cody Gakpo Transfer Latest as Tottenham and Manchester City Monitor Liverpool Forward

The latest transfer discussion from Fabrizio Romano placed Cody Gakpo firmly among the key late-window stories, with Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester City both mentioned in connection with the Liverpool forward.

With the market entering what Romano described as "24 crucial hours", the focus around Gakpo is now on Liverpool's position and whether any movement on incoming wide players changes the picture before the window closes.

Romano set the wider context by saying, "The market is moving things are happening and so it's going to be absolutely busy in the next days." He also stressed the timing, adding, "And also important to mention in seven days the window is closed and so it's going to be very important to see what happens in this hours."

Gakpo agreement with Tottenham already in place

The clearest update in the discussion concerned Tottenham's work on the player side. Romano said, "Talking about Gakpo guys. I maintain my information. He has an agreement on personal terms with Tottenham since July."

He then reinforced that stance by adding, "So Tottenham have an agreement with Gakpo and Tottenham are ready to give Gakpo what he wants."

That is the central detail in this story. According to Romano's information, Tottenham's groundwork with Gakpo has already been done for some time. The personal terms side is not being presented as an issue, and the London club are described as prepared to meet the player's expectations.

At this stage, that leaves the club-to-club element and, crucially, Liverpool's own decision-making as the key part of the situation.

Manchester City also in contact over Cody Gakpo

Romano also revealed that Manchester City have entered the conversation, though with a more tentative position at present.

That distinction matters. Tottenham are being described as having an agreement on personal terms, while City are framed as having held talks with the player's representatives without reaching any agreement.

Romano summarised it directly: "So let's maintain Tottenham there and then Manchester City also meeting with the agents."

In other words, Tottenham remain the more advanced suitor on the information provided, while Manchester City are in the background with contact made and the situation still open.

Liverpool stance depends on two winger arrivals

That is the condition around any potential departure. Romano then spelled it out even more clearly, saying, "If if Liverpool can get two wingers, Gakpo can go to Tottenham or to Man City."

He returned to the same point once more, underlining the threshold Liverpool would need to meet before authorising a sale: "And then it's important to mention that for Liverpool it's two wingers or no chance to give the green light."

From the discussion, there is no suggestion that Liverpool have already approved an exit. The message is that the situation is contingent. Gakpo's future, as Romano explained it, hinges on Liverpool securing two wingers. Without that, the green light does not arrive.

This leaves the story finely balanced in the final stretch of the window. Tottenham have an agreement with the player. Manchester City have spoken to his agents. Liverpool, however, remain the gatekeepers, and their stance is tied to recruitment.

Late-window picture becoming increasingly urgent

As Romano put it, "So many things are happening guys." In Gakpo's case, the essentials are straightforward. Tottenham are advanced on personal terms. Manchester City have made contact with the player's camp. Liverpool's approval depends on signing two wingers.

For now, that means no definitive conclusion has been reached. Yet the framework around the deal is now clear from Romano's update. "Tottenham have an agreement with Gakpo. Man City at the moment not yet. Let's see if they can agree."

Until Liverpool decide whether they can complete the required winger business, Gakpo remains one of the standout stories to watch in the closing days of the window. With Romano emphasising that the market is moving quickly and that the deadline is now close, this is a situation that appears set to run deep into the final stages.

articles.title: Fernando Alonso: Dutch GP strategy shows "I'm a very good driver"
articles.summary: The Aston Martin driver converted a one-stop strategy into a shock points finish
articles.body:
Fernando Alonso was full of self-praise at the Formula 1 Dutch Grand Prix, claiming that being "a very good driver" allowed him to convert a one-stop strategy into a shock points finish for Aston martin

The Spanish racer finished ninth at Zandvoort on Sunday from 18th on the grid, claiming his second points results of the 2026 campaign after 10th at Monaco in June.

The way impressive Alonso took ninth was very impressive too, as he got as far as the 34th lap on a pair of soft tyres before switching to hard rubber for the remainder of the 72-lap contest.

That was amid other drivers utilising at least a two-stop strategy, so the double world champion would wait patiently behind those set to pit and then make the most of the overcut in clean air.

"I'm a very good driver," said Alonso, when asked how he made it work. "That was not the plan. I think the plan was two stops and to go more conventional.

"But we need to sometimes deviate a little bit from what is normal. When we are in traffic, we cannot use our potential.

"We are faster in the corners and the people in front of us, we are slower on the straights, and we're stuck behind.

"So, as soon as we have free track in front of us, we try to use it, even if it's not the optimal performance and the optimal strategy and it's what we did today."

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing, Alexander Albon, Williams

Alonso's result came after Aston Martin brought a radically different chassis to Budapest at the prior round, before bringing an upgraded Honda engine to the Netherlands.

The updates have so far worked well as the British marque is no longer F1's slowest team - a tag that now belongs to newcomer Cadillac - but its Zandvoort weekend didn't start positively.

Alonso qualified last for the sprint race - team-mate Lance Stroll was in 19th - as he encountered driveability problems due to his straightline mode not working, causing him to lock up at Turn 1.

Stroll and the Spaniard eventually finished the sprint in 17th and 18th before a more respectable qualifying session for Sunday's race, taking 18th and 19th ahead of Haas and Cadillac.

Alonso reckons Aston Martin will not be "competitive" at the low-downforce Monza up next, but Zandvoort still represented "another step forward" for the Silverstone-based outfit.

"Especially on the chassis side," he added. "We brought four or five components here.

"Also, the Budapest package was understood in the break and with all the data available after the race, we fine-tuned a little bit the set-up around that new spec, plus the new parts.

"I think, now, we are optimising the chassis side and we are able to extract the maximum.

"On the engine, it's more difficult. I don't think we can be black and white on if we have more power or not.

"From the driver's side of things, you change circuit one month after the other race, so the drivability has been a difficult weekend.

"We're struggling with the downshift again and we're struggling with the engine braking corner to corner. So, it was a challenging weekend in that regard."

articles.title: Browns fans are angry at HC Todd Monken over Shedeur Sanders decision for final preseason game
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns QB Shedeur Sanders will not feature in their final preseason game against the New England Patriots, with the third-and-fourth-string QBs get...
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns QB Shedeur Sanders will not feature in their final preseason game against the New England Patriots , with the third-and-fourth-string QBs getting playing time instead.

After a competitive training camp, Sanders lost the QB1 battle to veteran Deshaun Watson for Week 1 against the Jacksonville Jaguars .

With the QB1 battle set, coach Todd Monken's decision not to play Sanders as QB1 for more reps in their final preseason game in favor of giving Dillon Gabriel an opportunity has raised some eyebrows.

Browns HC Todd Monken explains why Dillon Gabriel is playing and Shedeur Sanders isn't

Browns HC Monken spoke to the media on Tuesday after Sanders was confirmed to be out of the rotation for their preseason finale.

"We're not playing them because we'd like to see Dillon (Gabriel) more. It worked out last game, that was unfair to him. So, in order to do that, to see more of him and see Taylen (Green), there's just not enough reps."

"That's the reason, there's really nothing else. Just trying to see Taylen after he played pretty well in the limited reps he had against the Bills, and we want to see more of Dillon. It just hasn't worked out trying to get those other guys reps. That's the reason."

Gabriel started last season ahead of Sanders in the depth chart before losing his role to Sanders amid a rough rookie season. But with Shedeur going from QB3 to QB1 in one season last year, Gabriel could do the same with enough opportunity.

Browns fans are angry at Todd Monken for this decision

Browns fans were not happy to see this, as they would rather see Sanders get more reps than continue with the Gabriel experiment that went badly last season.

"It's like they are doing everything we don't want them to do in succession. Dillon Gabriel shouldn't be on an NFL roster, period," said a concerned fan .

"Cleveland Browns are a joke! Don't want Shedeur to play and completely embarrass them for picking Deshaun Watson over him!" said another fan .

articles.summary: The Philadelphia Phillies received some unfortunate news around the Arizona Diamondbacks superstar shortly after a head-turning decision.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Phillies have little room for error as they chase down the Atlanta Braves in the National League East, with every remaining series carrying significant postseason implications.

Philadelphia has surged at exactly the right time. The Phillies entered the final weeks of the regular season riding a nine-game winning streak and, even though that came to an end on Monday against the Seattle Mariners , that surge dramatically tightening the division race while also strengthening the team's position in the NL Wild Card picture.

"The Atlanta Braves saw their lead in the NL East whittled down to three games by the red-hot Philadelphia Phillies, potentially setting the stage for a competitive division race we didn't think we'd have down the stretch," Steve Gardner wrote for USA Today . "On the wave of their current nine-game winning streak, the Phils dramatically improved their playoff position over the past week, gaining serious ground on the Braves and moving into the NL's second wild-card spot with five weeks remaining in the regular season."

That makes Philadelphia's upcoming series in Arizona particularly interesting, especially with Diamondbacks star Ketel Marte set to return in time to challenge the Phillies ascension in the standings.

Yankees Voice Sends Retirement Update After 'Orgy' Comments Go Viral

Philadelphia Phillies Get Unfortunate Ketel Marte Update Before Arizona Diamondbacks Series

Marte has been at the center of an unusual saga, which began with an unexplained absence before a matchup with the Boston Red Sox and escalated after he was spotted at a casino.

"The Ketel Marte saga took another turn Friday as photos surfaced on social media showing the Diamondbacks second baseman at a local casino during the team's home game against the Reds ," Mike Axisa reported for CBS Sports . "Marte is currently on the injured list with a knee issue. He was initially placed on the restricted list after failing to show up for a game against the Red Sox in Boston on Monday."

Though Marte went viral for spending his recovery time at a casino after leaving his team, the Diamondbacks have indicated that he will be welcomed back to the lineup when he's healthy. And the Phillies have no learned they can expect that return to come when they face the Diamondbacks at the start of next week.

"Ketel Marte is tentatively expected to be activated next Tuesday, when the D-backs open their series against the Phillies in Arizona," MLB insider Francys Romero reported on X . "The infielder began his knee rehab last Friday in Arizona, putting him on track for a potential return."

The timing adds an extra challenge for a Phillies team looking to make up some ground in the division race with time running out.

Dodgers World Series Champion, Key To Tarik Skubal Trade, Suddenly Ends Career

Philadelphia Phillies Get Ketel Marte Update At Critical Juncture

Marte's potential return would give the Diamondbacks one of its most accomplished players back in the lineup, even if some teammates hold hard feelings over his sudden disappearance. He finished third in NL MVP voting in 2024 and has made an All-Star and won a Silver Slugger Award in both 2024 and 2025.

For the Phillies, the objective is straightforward: keep winning and put pressure on Atlanta. But the upcoming trip to Arizona could present an additional challenge if Marte does return as expected.

articles.title: Bayern Munich extends Max Eberl and Jan-Christian Dreesen contracts through 2029

articles.body:
MUNICH (AP) — Bayern Munich has extended the contracts of board member for sport Max Eberl and chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen through June 2029.

The Bavarian powerhouse announced the extensions after its supervisory board meeting late Tuesday, when it reiterated its faith in Eberl and Dreesen to continue in their roles.

"Our board is ideally positioned to drive FC Bayern forward both in sporting and commercial terms and to maintain its leading position in Europe," the club said.

The 52-year-old Eberl had a challenging start after taking over Bayern's transfer dealings in February 2024 . He endured a long search for a new coach after getting rejections from Xabi Alonso, Julian Nagelsmann and Ralf Rangnick. He then even tried and failed to convince outgoing coach Thomas Tuchel to stay.

Eberl eventually settled on Vincent Kompany , a decision that has proved inspired with the former Manchester City captain leading Bayern to back-to-back Bundesliga titles and a league and cup double last season.

Bayern appointed Dreesen as CEO in May 202 3 after dismissing his predecessor Oliver Kahn . The 58-year-old Dreesen had been vice chairman of the supervisory board since 2014 after joining Bayern as chief financial officer from the banking sector the year before.

NEW YORK, Aug 25 (Reuters) - Top seeds Novak Djokovic and Aryna Sabalenka suffered an early exit from the U.S. Open mixed doubles on Tuesday, falling 1-4 4-2 10-2 to Henry Patten and Katerina Siniakova in their opening match.

Djokovic, a 24-times Grand Slam singles champion, and four-times major winner Sabalenka made a strong start by taking the opening set. But Patten and doubles specialist Siniakova hit back to claim the second before dominating the tiebreak to secure a place in the quarter-finals.

Siniakova sealed the upset in style with an ace out wide on match point, ending the tournament hopes of the star-studded pairing.

"It wasn't looking very good for a while, in this format we play one bad game and all of a sudden the first set's gone," Patten said.

"We knew the same could happen in the second, and we played an amazing tiebreak. Kat acing Novak on match point was great."

The mixed doubles championship is once again being staged in the week before the singles main draw, after organisers revamped the format last year to attract more leading singles players by reducing the field and giving the event a standalone slot on the calendar.

The revamped format proved a commercial success in its debut year, drawing sellout crowds and attracting many of the sport's biggest singles names despite criticism from some doubles specialists, who argued it marginalised established pairings.

Italian duo Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori went on to retain the title by defeating Iga Swiatek and Casper Ruud in last year's final.

articles.title: What’s next for Shedeur Sanders after Deshaun Watson named Browns QB1?
articles.summary: Browns coach Todd Monken said Shedeur Sanders understands 'the long game." What does that look like after Deshaun Watson was named QB1?
articles.body:
The most-talked-about quarterback battle of NFL training camp was settled Monday when Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken announced Deshaun Watson as the team's starting quarterback over Shedeur Sanders .

Watson being named starter is a controversial decision . The embattled quarterback has fallen short of expectations following a record-breaking five-year, $230 million fully guaranteed contract he signed in March of 2022. Still, Monken said Watson gives the Browns the "best chance to move the ball and score points."

The Browns are scheduled to play their final preseason game on Thursday, Aug. 27, against the New England Patriots . Neither Watson nor Sanders is expected to play in Cleveland's preseason finale as they already solidified their roster spots.

Sanders is slated to be No. 2 on the Browns' quarterback depth chart behind Watson. Sanders started seven games as a rookie last year and was even an alternate selection to the Pro Bowl.

Monken told reporters he informed Sanders of the Browns' quarterback decision on Monday and the second-year quarterback handled the news with professionalism.

Shedeur Sanders' journey from college football to Browns quarterback

"He was awesome. You talk about someone that really understands the long game," Monken said. "That really I think that has come to understand the long game. What are we really in this for? What am I in it for? To have the Browns be an organization that people aspire to be, right? The long game. Where do we want to be in the long term?

"He understands that as well as a quarterback. Where he was at, where he's at now (and) where he wants to get to. That is what's so awesome about Shedeur understanding that. We met (Monday) morning for a good long time and all he had was a smile on his face because he understands what's really in front of him. He's gonna work his butt off to get better and he has already."

NANCY ARMOUR: The Browns picked Deshaun Watson over their future. Good luck with that | Opinion

Does Shedeur Sanders still have chance to start for the Browns?

NFL coaches often say it's a week-to-week league. It's often labeled as "coach speak," but there is a lot of truth to those words. Even though Watson was named the Browns starter, his job as QB1 isn't permanent.

The Browns begin the regular season with road games against the Jacksonville Jaguars and Tampa Bay Buccaneers before their home opener against the Carolina Panthers . If the Browns get off to a slow start or Watson performs similarly to his 19 previous career games in Cleveland, Monken could promote Sanders to starter.

It would be logical for the Browns to start Watson to begin the season and then switch to Sanders to finish out the year. It's typically an easier transition to start a veteran quarterback before turning to a younger signal-caller.

It's important for Sanders to stay focused and perform well in practice as he takes No. 2 quarterback reps and continue his development as a QB. There's a good chance his days as a starter in Cleveland are far from over.

"I think Shedeur has done a great job," Monken said. "He's come a long way and we're excited about his future."

articles.title: Commanders disrespected in ESPN's positional rankings
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders were disrespected in ESPN's positional rankings, ranked as one of the worst teams in the NFL with one of the worst running back roo...
articles.body:
ESPN's Mike Clay recently came out with his annual positional rankings ahead of the 2026 season. Clay doesn't think much of the Washington Commanders , with Washington falling to the bottom of the rankings at every position except quarterback, and receiving an overall rating of No. 24.

Washington's highest ranking was quarterback at No. 8. This is not surprising given the promise surrounding quarterback Jayden Daniels . They also have a solid backup in Marcus Mariota . So it is understandable why the Commanders' quarterback room ranks in the top 10 in the league.

Lowest Rankings - Running Back (No. 31) and Offensive Line (No. 31)

Both the Commanders running back room and offensive line room were ranked next-to-last. This ranking for the running back room is not exactly surprising. Washington had one of the best rushing offenses in the NFL last season, finishing in the top-five in rushing yards and top-10 in rushing touchdowns. Even with their rushing success last season, they decided to add a new backup in Rachaad White . Jacory Croskey-Merritt , who led Washington in rushing yards last season, will remain the top back. Croskey-Merritt and White are not the most well-known running backs in the NFL, but they should certainly be a productive duo given Washington's success in the run game last season. Therefore, Clay's rankings of the Commanders' running backs seem rather inaccurate.

His ranking of the offensive line, however, is in line with some other websites, such as Pro Football Focus , which ranked Washington's offensive line as the worst in the league due to the loss of left tackle Laremy Tunsil Jr for the majority of the season. There have also been injury concerns with the Commanders' center, Nick Allegretti , throughout training camp. Unless Washington adds depth to the offensive line before the season begins, this unit could really struggle.

Most Surprising Ranking - Wide Receiver (No. 22)

Besides the low ranking for the running back room, the ranking for the wide receiver group is also shocking. Washington had one of the worst passing offenses last season, but that is partly because Jayden Daniels and top wide receiver Terry McLaurin were out most of the season. Deebo Samuel led the Commanders in receiving last season, and while he is gone, Washington still has McLaurin; they signed Stefon Diggs and drafted promising rookie Antonio Williams . Depth receiver Luke McCaffrey is also still on the roster. There are concerns about McLaurin's and Diggs' ages because they are both in their 30s. However, that doesn't seem relevant, since both are still elite receivers in this league.

Also, when you look at the teams ahead of Washington, not all of them have better wide receivers than the Commanders. For example, the Arizona Cardinals ' wide receivers rank above Washington's. Their leading receiver last season was a tight end; their top receiver on the roster is Marvin Harrison Jr who has yet to live up to his expectations coming out of college. So, looking at the rankings, ranking Washington's receivers at No. 22 in the league does not make sense.

Saying Washington is going to be one of the worst teams in the league seems shocking. Among the teams ranked ahead of the Commanders are the New York Jets , who do not even have a solid quarterback situation. Washington is also ranked the lowest of any team in the NFC East, with the Philadelphia Eagles at No. 3, the Dallas Cowboys at No. 9, and the New York Giants at No. 23. This is a team that made the NFC Championship in 2024, and they have some key pieces from that 2024 team. The Commanders shouldn't be in the bottom half of the league or last in their division.

articles.title: 'OBACHT' with an even clearer design
articles.summary: FC Bayern remains steadfast in its commitment to ensuring a safe, respectful and discrimination-free stadium experience: three years after the launch of ‘OBA...
articles.body:
FC Bayern remains steadfast in its commitment to ensuring a safe, respectful and discrimination-free stadium experience: three years after the launch of 'OBACHT' ('watch out'), the club's awareness concept, the design has now been comprehensively revised and further developed to make it even clearer and easier to understand.

Three years of experience and responsibility

For the past three years, OBACHT has been an integral part of FC Bayern's home matches at the Allianz Arena. During this period, a wealth of experience has been gained, and feedback from fans and experts has been gathered and analysed. These insights have been incorporated into the further development of the concept.

What began as an initiative at the fans' request has since been rolled out to other venues, such as the FC Bayern Campus and BMW Park. It was also adopted by UEFA, the European football governing body, for the 2024 European Championship.

The aim is to foster a strong culture of watching out for one another at all FC Bayern venues and to make attending home matches even safer and more inclusive.

On matchdays, the OBACHT team can also be contacted via the Allianz Arena app.

OBACHT – look out for one another, safeguard one another

In this FC Bayern initiative, the Bavarian term 'OBACHT' stands for looking out for one another, keeping an eye on one another, supporting and respecting one another – and ensuring that qualified help is on hand should anyone need it.

FC Bayern thus recognises that tackling transgressive and discriminatory behaviour must be an ever-present and and indispensable priority. OBACHT raises awareness: looking away is not an option; not looking away is a stance.

Due to its history, its values and its social responsibility, FC Bayern takes a clear and unequivocal stand in favour of diversity, openness and tolerance. To this end, the German champions are committed to taking concrete action and launching initiatives to combat all forms of discrimination, most notably through their ' Red against Racism ' initiative.

Spaces for everyone – at the Arena, BMW Park and the Campus

Everyone should feel comfortable and safe at FC Bayern's match venues and club facilities. The club aims to create spaces for everyone and to foster a culture of being watchful.

OBACHT helps to ensure a safer stadium experience for everyone, irrespective of their background, religion, identity, sexual orientation or gender.

Working with the Südkurve and KIT München

FC Bayern developed OBACHT in collaboration with representatives from the Südkurve München (Munich South Stand) and the Fanprojekt München (Munich fan project), which is run by the non-profit organisation AWO München Stadt ( Munich City Workers' Welfare Association). This close collaboration with the fan community continues: the Südkurve remains an important partner in the further development of the concept to this day, contributing insights and experiences from the stands.

The KIT -München or Munich Crisis Intervention Team, run by the Arbeiter-Samariter-Bund (Workers' Samaritan Foundation), operates as the primary OBACHT team, carrying out awareness-raising work on matchdays, and is not bound by any instructions from the club.

The collaboration with KIT München has been further strengthened through the revised version of OBACHT: processes have been streamlined, responsibilities more clearly defined and the team's visibility to visitors enhanced, not least through the new design and clearer communication materials.

Be watchful together – put OBACHT into practice

OBACHT is more than just a concept on paper or a sign in the Arena: it is lived attitude.

FC Bayern expects all visitors , club members, players, staff and supporters to embody this ethos as part of the club. Together, we can ensure that FC Bayern's venues are places where everyone feels safe and respected.

But when healthy, this could be one of the best starting units in football.

On the opposite side of Gardner is Charvarius Ward , who is going into his second season with Indianapolis. However, he only played seven games with the Colts last year due to injuries, although he was still quite impactful when on the field, allowing a completion rate of just 56% when targeted.

Ward's best season was back in 2024 when he was a Pro-Bowler and second-team All-Pro. That season, he recorded five interceptions and defended 23 total passes.

Overall, Indianapolis should live up to its top-10 ranking at cornerback as long as Gardner and Ward stay healthy.

Villa are long-time admirers of Kofane, who joined Leverkusen from Albacete last summer.

His first season in Germany yielded seven goals and nine assists in 44 appearances across all competitions.

His performances earned him a place in Cameroon's squad for the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON), where they reached the quarter-final stage.

Villa are in the market for a potential replacement for Ollie Watkins , who is angling for a move to Saudi Pro League giants Al-Hilal.

They have rejected multiple bids, but Al-Hilal have an agreement with the player on personal terms.

Manager Unai Emery is unwilling to go through the season with Tammy Abraham and Brian Madjo as his options to lead the line.

Chelsea star Nicolas Jackson is also among their targets. He previously played under Emery at Villarreal .

They have had an approach turned down for Crystal Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta .

Villa should push the boat out for Jackson

Jackson is the most realistic choice for Villa. He has a respectable record of 24 goals and ten assists in 65 Premier League appearances.

The 25-year-old is familiar with the demands of Premier League football and understands how Emery works.

Kofane and Mateta would not be plug-and-play options for Emery, particularly as they would not have the luxury of pre-season training under him.

Jackson's selfless running and willingness to stretch defences make him the ideal fit for Villa.

With Villa set to compete on four fronts this season, they need a forward who can hit the ground running.

Jackson fits the bill and they must do whatever it takes to sign him before the transfer window closes.

articles.title: Youngsters 'not ready' says Watford boss Dionisi

articles.body:
Watford boss Alessio Dionisi admits his young players are not yet ready for the first-team after their humbling defeat by League One side Peterborough United in the Carabao Cup.

The Posh ran riot in a 5-1 thrashing at Vicarage Road against a youthful Hornets side after Watford made a promising start to the league campaign under new head coach Dionisi, picking up four points in the first two games.

"I'm not happy, we're not happy but this is football. Yesterday, the young boys worked well [in training] but the official match is different," Dionisi told BBC Three Counties Radio.

"For them, it is difficult because [they] are not ready to stay in the first-team but, for me, it's not a problem. It is important for everyone to prepare for the next match against West Ham because it will be very, very difficult for us."

Dionisi made 11 changes from the side that started Saturday's Championship 1-1 draw at Wrexham , naming two 17-year-old's and eight players under the age of 20 as his side were comprehensively dumped out of the cup in the second round.

"I am sorry for our supporters but, for me, there wasn't another possibility for us to play every three days with the same line-up. It is impossible," said Dionisi.

"The result is terrible but, in this moment, we prefer to choose to prepare [for] the Championship [over the Carabao Cup].

"We need new players to complete this team. We need new players with experience but we will work with what we have."

Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies quickly shut down two theories about Max Verstappen 's contract extension that were put forward by Nico Rosberg .

Four-time F1 world champion Verstappen signed a new contract with Red Bull until 2030 last week, which will extend the Dutch driver's partnership with the team to 15 years if he sees out his deal.

Rosberg, the world champion in Verstappen's debut Red Bull year in 2016, was in conversation with Mekies on the grid at the Dutch Grand Prix in Zandvoort when he put the 28-year-old's extension down to two reasons: a reported $80m-a-year deal and the culture Mekies has installed at the team since taking over from Christian Horner last year.

Yet in response, Mekies said: "So, both statements are not correct. It's down really to the trust that Max has in the 2,000 people we have in Milton Keynes [Red Bul HQ], chassis side, PU [power unit] side, and he knows what our people are capable of and he has chosen to put his trust in us for the future.

"So, we will try to pay him back for that. He's much more than just the fastest driver in the world for us and we'll try to make sure we give him a fast car as soon as possible."

Verstappen's future was shrouded in uncertainty given his dissatisfaction with this generation of car, alongside interest from Mercedes and McLaren, but the Dutchman has opted to remain with the only team he's ever known.

"It's phenomenal news, for the team of course, but also for us as a sport as a whole," Mekies added.

"It has been a great few weeks of discussions. From day one, Max said, 'I want to stay with you guys.' When we finally concluded everything, I said, 'Well, I thought you always wanted to stay anyway!'

"Jokes aside, we take the trust he is putting in us very, very seriously. It gives us a huge responsibility in terms of providing him with a package that he will need to fight for wins again.

"But there is nothing that we want more at Red Bull Racing than to come back to the top spot as soon as possible and we know that is also what Max wants."

Verstappen will be looking to bounce back following his massive first-lap crash at the Dutch Grand Prix at the next round in Monza (6 September).

articles.title: Franco Colapinto Pins Monza Hopes on Alpine’s Missing Upgrades: “Excited for the Future”
articles.summary: The 2026 Dutch Grand Prix proved to be a highly challenging weekend for Franco Colapinto, who crossed the finish line in 14th place while navigating treacher...
articles.body:
The 2026 Dutch Grand Prix proved to be a highly challenging weekend for Franco Colapinto , who crossed the finish line in 14th place while navigating treacherous, mixed conditions at Circuit Zandvoort. However, the Argentine driver's struggles were exacerbated by a significant mechanical discrepancy within the Alpine garage. While his teammate Pierre Gasly was equipped with the team's latest aerodynamic upgrade package and managed to salvage a championship point in 10th place, Colapinto was forced to battle the elements in older machinery.

Despite the obvious frustration of racing at a technical disadvantage, Colapinto told the media that he remains highly optimistic about his prospects for the upcoming Italian Grand Prix, where his car will finally receive the highly anticipated parts.

Colapinto on Making Moves Without the Upgrades

Zandvoort's sweeping, banked corners and unpredictable weather made it incredibly difficult for drivers to find a consistent rhythm. Despite lacking the ultimate pace of the updated Alpine, Colapinto still managed to execute several impressive overtakes during the wettest parts of the Grand Prix.

"It was difficult, but I think it was a good opportunity to make the moves, and I overtook four cars, so in those wet conditions, yeah, it was good to make some moves," Colapinto told the media.

However, the reality of the machinery deficit ultimately capped his progression through the midfield. He admitted that while the racecraft was satisfying, missing out on the points was a tough pill to swallow, particularly when seeing the success on the other side of the garage.

"But, of course, a bit annoying with the result, but at the end of the day, you know, we came without the upgrades, and it was tricky to score points," he explained. Noting Gasly's performance—Colapinto acknowledged the sheer value of the new parts. "Pierre was P10, so scored a point, which is positive, but for us, it was a bit tricky."

The Formula 1 paddock now heads straight to the high-speed "Temple of Speed" at Monza. As a pure power circuit requiring ultra-low downforce setups, aerodynamic efficiency is absolutely vital to remain competitive.

When asked about the upgrade situation and how frustrated he was to wait another week, Colapinto chose to focus entirely on the positives of the incoming development. Rather than dwelling on the Zandvoort disadvantage, the Alpine driver believes the new package will transform his race pace.

"Yeah, well, looking forward to the upgrades," Colapinto concluded. "I think they are a very big step, so excited for the future."

With Alpine fighting desperately for midfield supremacy in the Constructors' Championship, equipping both drivers with the full upgrade package could be the exact catalyst they need to consistently challenge for points across the European leg.

articles.title: Are you concerned by Man City 'fire sale'?
articles.summary: City boss Enzo Maresca made it quite clear during Friday's pre-match news conference that any player that is unhappy at the club is free to leave.  Maresca r...
articles.body:
Some of you have been sending questions in and Mathew asked me if Manchester City are having a "fire sale" and if the club are "tightening their belt for a specific reason".

City boss Enzo Maresca made it quite clear during Friday's pre-match news conference that any player that is unhappy at the club is free to leave.

Maresca revealed that Savio had said "from day one" that he wanted to move, while Omar Marmoush has been unhappy with the amount of gametime he has had since his move from Eintracht Frankfurt . He is too good a player to be playing second fiddle to Erling Haaland .

Are you concerned with the exits? Tell us

Tijjani Reijnders and Nico Gonzalez have both failed to nail down first-team places and the club stance has always been, if a bid comes in that matches the valuation of a player, they are free to go if they wish.

City bought Reijnders for £46.5m last summer and made a £6.5m profit on him, while they recouped most of what they paid for Gonzalez last January.

Elliot Anderson has already come in, a deal has been agreed for both Ayyoub Bouaddi and Allan Elias, while speculation around signing Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea has not gone away.

I'm expecting City and director of football Hugo Viana to do some deals before the end of the transfer window.

articles.summary: New Manchester City signing Ayyoub Bouaddi says it is a "dream" to join "the best club in the world".  The 18-year-old Morocco midfielder has moved from Lill...
articles.body:
New Manchester City signing Ayyoub Bouaddi says it is a "dream" to join "the best club in the world".

The 18-year-old Morocco midfielder has moved from Lille in a £85.6m deal and signed a five-year deal with City.

Enzo Maresca's side moved to sign Bouaddi after selling central midfielders Rodri to Barcelona in a £65m deal, Tijjani Reinders to Al-Qadsiah for £52m and agreeing to let Nico Gonzalez join Newcastle in a deal worth up to £52m.

"This is a very special day for me and my family," Bouaddi said on the move.

"Manchester City are, for me, the best club in the world. It's a dream to be here and be able to call myself a City player. I have spent most of my life working hard to become the best player I can be and reach the top of the game.

"I've watched City for many years, and I love their style of play. City always try and play quality football. And they have shown they are winners – this club feels like it's built to win.

"I have plenty of improving to do. I am only 18. This is undoubtedly the best place for me to do that.

"This club demands trophies and I will give everything to make sure we are challenging for every title."

Bouaddi impressed at this summer's World Cup - starting five of Morocco's six matches in their run to the quarter-finals - after becoming a key member of Lille's side in Ligue 1 .

City Director of Football Hugo Viana added: "Ayyoub's potential is extremely high - a player equipped with everything a top midfielder needs.

"At just 18, he already has outstanding football intelligence and that will only improve under the guidance of Enzo.

"We have watched him very, very closely and throughout that process we have become increasingly convinced he is a huge talent who will thrive at City."

articles.body:
Manchester City have signed teenage Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in a five-year deal the French club said Wednesday was worth 100 million euros (£86 million, $117 million).

City moved for Bouaddi after selling Spain's World Cup winning captain Rodri to Barcelona and Tijjani Reijnders to Al-Qadsiah, with Nico Gonzalez also poised to leave the Etihad.

The 18-year-old rising star was one of the stand-out players at the recent World Cup, helping Morocco reach the quarter-finals before they were beaten by France.

Bouaddi will join England's Elliot Anderson in City's revamped midfield.

"This is a very special day for me and my family," Bouaddi said in a statement on the City website.

"Manchester City are, for me, the best Club in the world.

"It's a dream to be here and be able to call myself a City player. I have spent most of my life working hard to become the best player I can be and reach the top of the game.

"I've watched City for many years, and I love their style of play.

"City always try and play quality football. And they have shown they are winners –- this Club feels like it's built to win."

Enzo Maresca made central midfield a key area for new signings after replacing Pep Guardiola as City manager at the end of last season.

City are also believed to retain an interest in Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez , but the Blues set a recent deadline for bids for the £120 million-rated Argentine that passed without a deal being done.

City were thrashed 3-0 by Arsenal in the Community Shield, but they started their Premier League campaign with a 2-1 win at home to Bournemouth on Sunday.

The 18-year-old joins on a five-year contract, subject to international clearance, with City paying £81.4m upfront plus £4.2m in add-ons.

"I've watched City for many years, and I love their style of play. City always try and play quality football. And they have shown they are winners - this club feels like it's built to win."

Bouaddi made 96 appearances for Lille after making his debut in 2023, helping them finish third in Ligue 1 last season.

At the age of 16 he became the youngest footballer to ever play for the French side on his senior debut against Faroese club KI in the Europa League, before announcing himself on the world stage by playing a starring role in Lille's Champions League victory over Real Madrid in 2024.

Bouaddi will form part of a revamped midfield, with City already bringing in England midfielder Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116m.

Bouaddi functions as a deep-lying conductor and would complement Anderson, who is comfortable as a box-to-box midfielder as well as the number six role he plays for England .

City are also set to make an offer for Chelsea 's Argentina midfielder Enzo Fernandez but it remains to be seen whether a deal can be struck with the 25-year-old valued at £120m.

Bouaddi's signing comes after Brazilian winger Savinho , now known as Savio, joined Tottenham in a £75m deal earlier this week.

Spurs have also agreed a loan deal to sign City's Egypt forward Omar Marmoush , while Spain midfielder Nico Gonzalez is set to leave Maresca's side to join Newcastle in a £52m deal.

articles.title: Lake Travis, Vandegrift top our Class 6A rankings as we preview Central Texas high school football
articles.summary: Our 2026 high school football previews and district predictions for Class 6A include our first top-five rankings of the season, led by Lake Travis.
articles.body:
The American-Statesman takes a look at Class 6A districts around Central Texas as the high school football season gets underway.

Fab Five: Central Texas' top 5 teams from Class 6A

1. Lake Travis (14-1 last year, DI state semifinalist): The Cavs graduated 18 starters, but there's never a lack of talent. DBs Luca Antoun and Jeremiah Strong and LB Owen Aird lead what should be one of the area's best defenses.

This video created with the assistance of AI.

2. Vandegrift (12-2, DII state semifinalist): New QB Gavin Koester paces an offense that should thrive running the ball, and the Vipers are deep with talent at all three levels on defense.

3. Westlake (7-4, DII area round): There are more question marks than in the past decade for the Chaps. But like Lake Travis, Westlake always has talent. Wylie Nichols is one of Central Texas' better defensive backs.

4. Dripping Springs (12-2, DII regional finalist): Chase Ames is the area's most prolific 6A QB and has a massive offensive line to protect him. The Tigers seem primed for another double-digit win season.

5. Hutto (9-3, DI area round): WR/DB Jaiden Fields is one of the area's top three players. If the Hippos get good play from a new quarterback, the sky's the limit for the offense.

Our other playoff teams: Hutto, Cedar Park and East View

Notes: Cedar Park, East View, Leander and Rouse all make the jump to 6A, with Vista Ridge the district's seventh team. This district is also in Region III, which offers a much tougher playoff route than Region IV. … While Vandegrift and Hutto seem to be a level above the rest of the district, the battle for the last two playoff spots should be fierce. … Keep an eye on whether or not Vista Ridge makes the playoffs. If it does, along with Vandegrift, Cedar Park and Hutto, that would push the Vipers into DII. … East View safety Jalani Culpepper is receiving Power Four interest. … Cedar Park's David Cooper is the district's only returning starting QB. He threw for 1,925 yards and 19 TDs in 2025. … Hutto (Casey Walraven), Rouse (Mark Hopkins) and Leander (Ahmad Zaidan) all have new coaches.

Our other playoff teams: Westlake, Round Rock and Cedar Ridge

Key game: Lake Travis vs. Westlake (Oct. 23)

Notes: Westlake and Lake Travis move into a district with the five Round Rock ISD schools. … Westlake's Jackson Cook and Lake Travis' Jackson Koeppel are arguably the two best offensive linemen in Central Texas, with Cook committed to Texas. … Round Rock has something neither Westlake nor Lake Travis do: an experienced starter at quarterback. Dov Stickler returns after throwing for 1,850 yards and 15 TDs during the Dragons' final eight games. He also has one of the area's top WRs in TCU commit Dylan Jaeger. … Stony Point has a new coach in Dustin Pleasant after longtime coach Craig Chessher retired . … Cedar Ridge is looking for its first playoff appearance since 2022 and first winning season since 2021. QB Dylan Snoga accounted for 1,736 yards and 17 TDs as a junior. … Jerry Gardner is McNeil's new coach. … Westlake would need either Lake Travis or Round Rock to miss the playoffs to be in DI in the postseason.

Our other playoff teams: Bowie, Johnson and Hays

Key game: Dripping Springs vs. Bowie (Oct. 16)

Notes: Realignment strangely didn't put Dripping Springs in a district with nearby Lake Travis and Westlake, instead grouping the Tigers with fellow Hays County schools Johnson and Hays, Austin ISD's three 6A schools (Austin High, Bowie and Akins) and Del Valle. Hays moves up from 5A DI and Johnson returns to an Austin-centric district after playing south the last two years. … Dripping Springs is the overwhelming favorite, but don't count out Bowie. The Bulldogs return eight defensive starters and have a powerhouse RB in Rhys Moreno. … Johnson is the district's wildcard. The Jaguars missed the playoffs a year ago but welcome back QB Jonah Montgomery and eight other starters. … Austin High LB Ethan Kahle is arguably the best player the Central Texas public isn't aware of. He tallied 121 tackles in 2025 and leads the Maroons' hopes to reach the postseason. … Keep an eye on Hays RB Eyan Stigall. Hawks coach Mark Torres is high on his talent, and Stigall ran for 537 yards and seven TDs as a sophomore. … A DII regional final between Dripping Springs and Westlake seems likely.

articles.title: Man City complete record £86m deal for Rodri replacement
articles.summary: The Morocco international shone for Lille last term and continued his impressive run of form at the World Cup, with the 18-year-old now a key piece in the Ci...
articles.body:
Manchester City have signed Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille for £85m in a record deal for a teenager in Premier League history.

Bouaddi has signed a five-year contract at the Etihad Stadium, becomes their second midfield signing of the summer after Elliot Anderson .

City's midfield revamp has now cost over £200m – with Anderson a club record purchase at £85m – with the potential of a third arrival there and interest in Enzo Fernandez of Chelsea .

Bouaddi excelled in the World Cup for Morocco as a teenager and City see him as a talent with the ability to get better still.

Director of football Enzo Maresca said: "Ayyoub's potential is extremely high - a player equipped with everything a top midfielder needs.

"At just 18, he already has outstanding football intelligence and that will only improve under the guidance of Enzo [Maresca, the manager].

"We have watched him very, very closely and throughout that process we have become increasingly convinced he is a huge talent who will thrive at City."

Bouaddi, who was the youngest player in Lille's history, will be charged with replacing Rodri and Bernardo Silva , who have joined Barcelona and Real Madrid respectively.

City could lose four midfielders this summer, with Tijjani Reijnders moving to Al Qadsiah for £51m and Newcastle agreeing a £52m fee for Nico Gonzalez.

Bouaddi, who will take the No 32 shirt at City, said: "I am really, really happy – really proud to be here at one of the greatest clubs in the world.

"This is a very special day for me and my family. Manchester City are, for me, the best Club in the world. It's a dream to be here and be able to call myself a City player. I have spent most of my life working hard to become the best player I can be and reach the top of the game.

"I've watched City for many years, and I love their style of play. City always try and play quality football. And they have shown they are winners – this Club feels like it's built to win.

"The squad is world-class and Enzo is a top manager. And I'm really looking forward to playing at the Etihad Stadium, in front of all the fans.

"I think it was the right time because I was good in Lille, I felt very good, but I felt it was the right moment to step over and coming to City."

articles.title: Form the key in Swansea striker battle
articles.summary: Vitor Matos says his forwards will be judged purely on form as Zan Vipotnik, Adam Idah and Ross Stewart compete for game-time at Swansea City this season.  V...
articles.body:
Vitor Matos says his forwards will be judged purely on form as Zan Vipotnik , Adam Idah and Ross Stewart compete for game-time at Swansea City this season.

Vipotnik was the top scorer in the Championship in 2025-26, but his sparkling form last term did not save the Slovenia international from being left out of Matos' starting side in last weekend's draw with Sheffield United.

Vipotnik had begun Swansea's opening-day victory over Stoke City, but was substituted after a low-key display as Idah came on to Swansea's winner at the Bet365 Stadium.

Republic of Ireland international Idah was picked against the Blades and produced an effective display before Vipotnik and new recruit Ross Stewart featured as substitute.

"It's about performance, nothing more," said Swansea head coach Matos.

"That doesn't change for striker, midfielder or winger.

"Who we use, when they are all in shape and on their best moment , it will depend on the opposition. When one is in a better moment than the other, then it's about us taking the best of that one and then we keep moving, like in all the positions."

Questions remain over whether Vipotnik will still be a Swansea player after the transfer window closes next Tuesday.

Regardless of the transfer situation, Idah may be favourite to start at Derby County on Saturday given the solid shift he put in last time out.

"I think Adam gave us the physicality we knew we needed on that position because of the man marking and because of the one-v-one on the last line," Matos said.

"We didn't really connect the way we wanted to find him in the best moment, but he offered a lot.

"I think he was quite important to push the team to the opposition half and that's what we gained with him."
